newsitem.title: UK: IPE GAS OIL SEEN $2.50 LOWER, BRENT 10-15 CTS DOWN.
newsitem.headline: IPE GAS OIL SEEN $2.50 LOWER, BRENT 10-15 CTS DOWN.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures are expected to open weaker on Friday, extending the week's slide sparked by Iraq's return to the export market and sliding U.S. gasoline prices, brokers said.
Aug gas oil, which closed at $172.50 a tonne, was expected to open about $2.50 lower while Sept Brent was expected to begin trading about 10-15 cents below its Thursday settlement of $18.90 a barrel.
"I still think this market is going lower. People shouldn't have been too surprised by the recent selloff and there's little standing in the way of further losses," said a broker.
U.S. gasoline prices fell sharply on Thursday as talk of improving supply reversed a seasonal rally built on the back of particularly active driving season.

Rampant NYMEX gasoline futures and Iraq's absence from the crude market since late May were the two main motors for the summer rally which took prompt Brent crude to a 10-week high of $19.64 a barrel on Monday.
But this week has seen both supports removed.
"If we go below $18.80 on Brent then we could be heading for a much bigger drop," said a broker.
Interim support on August gas oil was pegged at $170.50.
On Wednesday, Iraq's oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said he expected exports to resume by mid-August.
Pricing formulas covering the renewed sales have been passed to the U.N. Security Council's sanctions committee which has until 1500 GMT on Friday to raise any objections.
Traders are bracing themselves for a flood of Iraqi crude starting next week, which would undermine spot market values of alternative crudes.
